selection: Both major prior-choice groups, with every published D/R/other/unsure percentage and the unreported nonresponse explicitly unknown. No outcome-selected subgroup or respondent records.
historical_evidence: Participation in 2024 is matched to official records; candidate choice was surveyed after that election, not administratively observed. The article says the month after and the exported workbook says the week after; exact historical interview dates are unverified.
current_evidence: September 28-October 4, 2026 House intentions including leaners, among current registered voters. This is not completed November choice, a fixed original 2024 coalition, or the selected 2026 electorate.
question_scope: CONG and CONGA normally insert district candidate names. The source retains generic party choices in Alaska/some Louisiana races, Missouri map litigation, unopposed races and one unknown district. No named statewide House race is inferred.
weights: ATP recruitment/selection and nonresponse/attrition adjustments, then wave calibration and 1st/99th percentile trimming. Native benchmarks include validated 2024 turnout/choice using FEC results, UF Election Lab turnout and 2023 ACS VEP. These are not 2026 electorate weights; no new 2024 reweighting or N26 scaling is applied.
study_identity: Independent American Trends Panel study, fielded by SSRS for Pew. A shared contractor does not make it the SSRS Voter Poll sample.
nonresponse_and_rounding: The workbook explicitly omits no-answer responses. A displayed four-response sum of 100 does not establish zero refusals. Unknown stays null; no renormalization or subtraction of unsure/nonresponse into nonvoting.
precision: Whole percentages are publisher-rounded descriptives, not exact population probabilities. Prior-group bases and joint design intervals were not supplied in these selected tables. The overall registered-voter 1.8 pp MoE is not assigned to prior groups or comparisons.
demographic_and_local_limits: The released workbook supplies separate demographic House preferences but not demographic-by-prior-vote joints. Do not multiply disconnected marginals or transfer Pew category definitions to other studies. No state/county/precinct allocation.
rights: Limited attributed factual excerpts, source receipts and our code only. Native report HTML/PDFs/figures and full workbook remain private and are not mirrored or relicensed. No respondent-level dataset or personal records acquired. No Pew endorsement is implied.
attribution: Pew Research Center, American Trends Panel Wave 200, survey September 28-October 4, 2026, published October 8, 2026.
